newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba rebuilds pre-revolutionary country club.
newsitem.headline: Cuba rebuilds pre-revolutionary country club.

text.p: Cuban authorities are rebuilding a symbol of pre-revolutionary privilege, the Havana Biltmore Yacht and Country Club, as a new sports club, a Cuban newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The remodelled Club Habana will also be a place for the affluent few since it will charge membership in dollars and will be aimed at diplomats and other foreign residents.

The weekly business newspaper Opciones said Wednesday that the the club was expected to open in mid-1998 and services would include massage facilities and exercise rooms, as well as a pool and mini-golf.
The Cuban state hotel and tourism chain Cubanacan is rebuilding the club and expects to recoup its investment in three years, Opciones said.
The Havana Biltmore Yacht and Country Club, which existed from 1928-58, was one of the best known of several exclusive clubs in Cuba before President Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution.
The club, an imposing mansion located in Havana's leafy residential district of Miramar, was used as a national sports school from 1959 until 1993, when it fell into disuse.
